summary:
Earth System & Climate Telemetry is an interactive website that lets visually impaired people explore climate data by listening instead of looking. A world map is divided into seven regions, and five criteria (glaciers, wildfires, drought, ocean and storms) each have their own button and their own sound, which mixes a sound effect with music. Pressing a criterion plays its sound and lights up the regions where it occurs, so listeners can connect each phenomenon to a place.

Each criterion also has an information text that can be read aloud, and a spoken guide gives a briefing for each region in one of three narrator voices. An assistant called Earth Copilot answers questions typed or spoken, reads its answers aloud, and understands voice commands such as “open Europe” or “play wildfires”. The site works in Turkish and English and supports keyboard navigation and screen readers.
details:
Our project is an interactive website that lets visually impaired people explore climate data by listening instead of looking. A world map is divided into seven regions, and five climate criteria (glaciers, wildfires, drought, ocean and storms) each have a button and a sound that mixes a sound effect with music. Pressing a criterion plays its sound and lights up the regions where it occurs. Each criterion also has an information text that can be read aloud, a spoken guide gives a briefing for each region, and a voice assistant answers typed or spoken questions and understands commands like “open Europe” or “play wildfires”.

Its main benefit is access. About 2.2 billion people live with a vision impairment, and 43 million are blind, yet climate data is almost always shown in maps and charts. Our site turns that data into sound, speech and text, so these learners can understand the climate crisis independently. We hope it also helps teachers, and that it shows how scientific data can be made accessible to everyone.

We built it as a single HTML file using JavaScript, React, Tailwind CSS and the Natural Earth map data. For sound we used the browser’s built-in speech tools (speech synthesis and speech recognition) and HTML audio. It needs no special hardware and runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari.

The creative part is the idea of a “music box for the Earth”: each climate phenomenon has its own sound identity, and the map lights up to show where it happens. We also gave the narration three distinct voices, and the music lowers automatically while someone speaks.

Our team considered accessibility first: keyboard navigation, screen-reader announcements, large buttons, and a key to stop all sound instantly. We offer Turkish and English, and because sound alone cannot carry precise facts, every criterion has a text that can be read aloud. We also kept the structure simple, with seven regions and five criteria, so it is easy to learn and remember.
